original_clauses.source_paraphrase: After Embodied announced its closure, customers were told that cloud-connected Moxie robots would stop functioning when the company’s servers shut down; families reported that children who had formed attachments would have to say goodbye.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A child-facing companion whose core interaction depends on provider infrastructure has an end-of-service boundary: termination and transition should account for the loss of that relational function and clearly identify what will and will not continue.

taxonomy_relationships.rationale: Reported child attachment and distress when the cloud-dependent companion was to stop functioning materially engage the relational-dependence boundary, but the reporting does not establish that Embodied optimised attachment to impair disengagement or that the shutdown itself resulted from such optimisation.

original_clauses.source_paraphrase: Some customers tried to develop an open-source alternative that might keep Moxie operating after Embodied’s servers closed, but the report said feasibility was uncertain.
original_clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A continuity path should be described according to what is actually available and to whom; an attempted community workaround should not be represented as a verified service transition.
